title: Naval Topic 12 生词 · 单词卡

cards.ex: An outcome is the result of something.
exs: The outcome was better than I expected.
We can't control every outcome.

src.t: The worst outcome in the world is not having self-esteem.

cards.ex: Self-esteem is how much you like and respect yourself.
exs: Kind words can boost a child's self-esteem.
Her self-esteem grew when her business grew.

src.t: The worst outcome in the world is not having self-esteem.

cards.ex: A tough one means a difficult question or problem.
exs: That's a tough one. Let me think.
Choosing a color is a tough one.

src.t: It’s a tough one.

cards.ex: A slot is a place or position, like a time slot or a spot in a group.
exs: I have a free slot at three.
That's the toughest slot to be in.

src.t: I look at the people who don’t like themselves and that’s the toughest slot because they’re always wrestling with themselves.

cards.ex: To wrestle with something means to struggle hard with it, like a problem or your feelings.
exs: I wrestled with the decision for weeks.
She wrestles with self-doubt.

src.t: I look at the people who don’t like themselves and that’s the toughest slot because they’re always wrestling with themselves.

cards.ex: The outside world means everything and everyone outside yourself or your home.
exs: After a week at home, I missed the outside world.
He hides from the outside world.

src.t: It’s hard enough to face the outside world, and no one’s going to like you more than you like yourself, so if you’re struggling with yourself then the outside world becomes an insurmountable challenge.

cards.ex: To struggle with something means to find it very hard.
exs: I struggle with fast English.
Many people struggle with money.

src.t: It’s hard enough to face the outside world, and no one’s going to like you more than you like yourself, so if you’re struggling with yourself then the outside world becomes an insurmountable challenge.

cards.ex: Insurmountable means too big or too hard to deal with.
exs: The problem felt insurmountable.
No challenge is insurmountable.

src.t: It’s hard enough to face the outside world, and no one’s going to like you more than you like yourself, so if you’re struggling with yourself then the outside world becomes an insurmountable challenge.

cards.ex: Low self-esteem means not liking or valuing yourself enough.
exs: Low self-esteem can hold you back.
He's shy because of low self-esteem.

src.t: It’s hard to say why people have low self-esteem.

cards.ex: Genetic means passed down from your parents through your genes.
exs: Eye color is genetic.
Is shyness genetic?

src.t: It might be genetic, it might just be circumstantial.

cards.zh: 环境造成的；偶然情况的
cards.ex: Circumstantial means caused by the situation you're in, not by your nature.
exs: Her stress is circumstantial; it's a busy month.
The problem may be circumstantial.

src.t: It might be genetic, it might just be circumstantial.

cards.ex: Unconditionally means without any conditions or limits.
exs: Parents should love their kids unconditionally.
Love yourself unconditionally.

src.t: A lot of times I think it’s because they just weren’t unconditionally loved as a child and that sort of seeps in at a deep core level, but self-esteem issues can be the most limiting.

cards.ex: To seep in means to slowly go into something, like water or a feeling.
exs: Rain seeped in through the window.
Doubt can seep in slowly.

src.t: A lot of times I think it’s because they just weren’t unconditionally loved as a child and that sort of seeps in at a deep core level, but self-esteem issues can be the most limiting.

cards.ex: The core is the center or the most important part.
exs: Honesty is at the core of my business.
It hurt me at my core.

src.t: A lot of times I think it’s because they just weren’t unconditionally loved as a child and that sort of seeps in at a deep core level, but self-esteem issues can be the most limiting.

cards.ex: Limiting means holding you back, not letting you grow.
exs: Fear is very limiting.
Limiting beliefs keep us small.

src.t: A lot of times I think it’s because they just weren’t unconditionally loved as a child and that sort of seeps in at a deep core level, but self-esteem issues can be the most limiting.

cards.ex: To some extent means partly, not completely.
exs: To some extent, I agree.
Luck matters to some extent.

src.t: One interesting thought is that to some extent self-esteem is a reputation you have with yourself.

cards.ex: A reputation is what people think of you.
exs: She has a great reputation in town.
Protect your reputation.

src.t: One interesting thought is that to some extent self-esteem is a reputation you have with yourself.

cards.ex: At all times means always.
exs: Keep your tools clean at all times.
Stay calm at all times.

src.t: You’re watching yourself at all times, you know what you’re doing and you have your own moral code.

cards.ex: A moral code is your own set of rules about right and wrong.
exs: Honesty is part of my moral code.
Everyone has a moral code.

src.t: You’re watching yourself at all times, you know what you’re doing and you have your own moral code.

cards.ex: To hold someone to a standard means to expect them to meet it.
exs: Don't hold others to rules you break yourself.
I hold myself to high standards.

src.t: Everyone has a different moral code, but if you don’t live up to your own moral code, the same code that you hold others to, it will damage your self-esteem.

cards.ex: To damage means to hurt or harm something.
exs: Strong glue can damage natural lashes.
Lies damage trust.

src.t: Everyone has a different moral code, but if you don’t live up to your own moral code, the same code that you hold others to, it will damage your self-esteem.

cards.ex: To live up to something means to meet a standard or promise.
exs: I want to live up to my own code.
The service lived up to the hype.

src.t: So perhaps one way to build up your self-esteem is to live up to your own code – very rigorously have one and then live up to it.

cards.ex: Rigorously means very carefully and strictly.
exs: I rigorously clean my tools.
Test it rigorously.

src.t: So perhaps one way to build up your self-esteem is to live up to your own code – very rigorously have one and then live up to it.

cards.ex: To raise means to lift or increase something.
exs: Helping others can raise your self-esteem.
We raised our prices.

src.t: Another way to raise your self-esteem might be to do things for others.

cards.ex: To look back on something means to think about it from the past.
exs: I look back on my first year with a smile.
When you look back on your life, what matters?

src.t: If I look back on my life and what are the moments that I’m actually proud of, they’re very far and few between.

cards.ex: Proud of means feeling good about something you or someone close to you did.
exs: I'm proud of my work.
My mom is proud of me.

src.t: If I look back on my life and what are the moments that I’m actually proud of, they’re very far and few between.

cards.ex: Far and few between (also few and far between) means very rare.
exs: Quiet days are far and few between.
Good clients like her are few and far between.

src.t: If I look back on my life and what are the moments that I’m actually proud of, they’re very far and few between.

cards.ex: To expect means to think something will happen.
exs: I didn't expect so many clients.
What did you expect?

src.t: It’s not that often and it’s not the things you would expect – it’s not the material success, it’s not having learned this thing or that.

cards.ex: Material success means having money and nice things.
exs: Material success isn't everything.
He has material success but no time.

src.t: It’s not that often and it’s not the things you would expect – it’s not the material success, it’s not having learned this thing or that.

cards.ex: To make a sacrifice means to give up something you want for someone or something more important.
exs: She made a sacrifice for her kids.
I made a sacrifice to open my studio.

src.t: It’s when I made a sacrifice for somebody or something that I loved.

cards.ex: Ironically means in a way that is the opposite of what you would expect.
exs: Ironically, I rest better when I'm busy.
Ironically, the cheapest glue worked best.

src.t: That’s when I’m actually, ironically, most proud.

cards.ex: Explicit means clear and directly stated, done on purpose.
exs: Give explicit aftercare instructions.
It was an explicit choice.

src.t: Now that’s through an explicit mental exercise, but I’ll bet you at some level I’m recording that implicitly.

cards.ex: Implicitly means without saying it directly, happening below your awareness.
exs: I implicitly trust her.
We learn many rules implicitly.

src.t: Now that’s through an explicit mental exercise, but I’ll bet you at some level I’m recording that implicitly.

cards.ex: At some level means in some way, maybe deep inside.
exs: At some level, I knew it was wrong.
At some level, everyone wants respect.

src.t: Now that’s through an explicit mental exercise, but I’ll bet you at some level I’m recording that implicitly.

cards.ex: To express means to show a feeling or idea.
exs: Express love through actions.
I can't express how happy I am.

src.t: So that tells me that even if I am not being loved, the way to create love is to give love, to express love through sacrifice and through duty.

cards.ex: A duty is something you must do because it's right or it's your job.
exs: It's my duty to keep clients safe.
Family duty matters to her.

src.t: So that tells me that even if I am not being loved, the way to create love is to give love, to express love through sacrifice and through duty.

cards.ex: To build up means to make something stronger over time.
exs: Build up your confidence slowly.
She built up her savings.

src.t: And so I think doing things like that can build up your self-esteem really fast.

cards.ex: A sacrifice is giving up something you value for something more important.
exs: Parents make many sacrifices.
I sacrificed my weekends for my studio.

src.t: It’s interesting when you talk about sacrifice, because a lot of the time people say, “I sacrificed so much for my job.”

cards.ex: Genuinely means really and truly.
exs: I'm genuinely happy for you.
She genuinely cares.

src.t: It’s like, yeah, but that was you sacrificing something that you wanted less for something that you wanted more, as opposed to genuinely taking some sort of cost.

cards.ex: A cost is what you must give or lose to get something.
exs: Every choice has a cost.
The cost of fame is privacy.

src.t: It’s like, yeah, but that was you sacrificing something that you wanted less for something that you wanted more, as opposed to genuinely taking some sort of cost.
